newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count up 27 to 988 in week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count up 27 to 988 in week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 988 as of June 6, up 27 from the prior week and 207 above the year-ago total of 781, Baker Hughes Inc reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by 26 to 842, while rigs working offshore was up one at 120. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose remained at 26.
Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Texas, which was up by seven. Louisiana was up by four and New Mexico down by four.
The Gulf of Mexico rig count rose two to 116.
A total of 404 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up nine from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by 18 to 580, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at four.
There were 200 rigs drilling directionally, 75 drilling horizontally and 713 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 29 to 286, versus 228 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
